last_outcome: M1-02 done (iteration 14): scripts/build-engine.mjs (esbuild, ADR-010) bundles packages/flight-sim to a committed supabase/functions/_shared/flight-sim.js so the Deno release-pigeon Edge Function can import the one real flight-physics implementation (ADR-001) without pnpm workspace resolution; CI regenerates it and fails on git diff. supabase/functions/release-pigeon/handler.ts is the adapter's business logic kept as plain data-in/data-out TypeScript (no Deno globals) so it runs under a new `functions` Jest project with a stubbed ReleaseDeps; index.ts is the thin, untestable-here Deno bootstrap (Request/Response, a live Supabase client, npm:@supabase/supabase-js@2). /code-review --effort high caught a real gap self-review missed: handleRelease originally trusted conversationId/recipientId from the request without checking the authenticated sender was actually a conversation member - release_pigeon is revoked from `authenticated` precisely so this adapter is the only guard standing between a JSON body and a service-role call, so this would have let any authenticated user forge a flight into an arbitrary conversation. Fixed same iteration with a getConversationMemberIds dependency, required both ids to be members, before any loft is even queried. Filed M1-10 as a follow-up: handleRelease never computes isFirstEverFlight, so planFlight's already-correct 'first bird never dies' short-circuit is unreachable from the one real release path. gate:tests floor raised 127 -> 136.
